chain: Glue holds lid skin in a fold
eyelid-glue.text: Users apply it to create a temporary double eyelid, giving a visible crease and a more open look for the day. It is used as a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery. Published research on the product itself is limited.

chain: Tape pulls outer corner to temple
canthal-tilt-tape-lateral-eye-lift-tape.text: Looksmaxxers use it to lift the outer eye corners for a more upward-angled, positive canthal tilt look while it is worn. The change in angle is visible straight away; no studies on the tape were found.

winged-eyeliner-for-tilt.text: The wing is drawn to suggest an upturned outer eye corner, giving the eyes a more tilted, defined shape as soon as it is applied. It is a standard makeup technique; its effect on perceived tilt has not been formally studied.

chain: Lash line looks darker and denser
Eyes look deeper and more defined
tightlining-waterline-liner.text: Users apply liner at the waterline to make lashes look fuller and the eyes look more defined, visible immediately. It is popular in makeup and grooming circles; its effect on perceived eye depth has not been studied.

guyliner-kohl.text: Men use eyeliner or kohl to make the eyes look darker and more intense, an effect visible as soon as it is applied. The style runs from ancient Egyptian use to 2000s emo guyliner. Appearance effects are observable rather than trial-tested.

eyelash-growth-serum-peptide-otc.text: Users apply these drug-free serums hoping for longer, thicker lashes that frame the eyes. They are popular in forums and sold as alternatives to prescription prostaglandin products. Published trials of the peptide versions were not found.

lash-extensions.text: Users get them for longer, fuller, curled lashes that make the eyes look larger and more defined, a change visible as soon as they are applied. A set typically lasts a few weeks. The result is cosmetic and observable directly.

lash-tint.text: Users get lashes dyed so they look darker and fuller without mascara, a visible change for several weeks. It is a common salon service. The effect is cosmetic and directly observable.

eyebrow-growth-serum.text: Users apply peptide or botanical serums hoping to make sparse brows look denser and fuller, often alongside castor oil, microneedling or minoxidil. Published evidence centres on prescription bimatoprost rather than the over-the-counter products.

chain: Oil brushed on brows and lashes
Hair believed to thicken or lengthen
castor-oil-on-brows-lashes.text: Practitioners brush castor oil on brows and lashes as a folk remedy for thicker, longer hair, and it is popular online. The growth claim has not been tested in trials; anecdote drives its use.

eyebrow-microblading.text: Users get it to fill thin or uneven brows with hair-like strokes, producing fuller, darker brows that last a long time. The visible result is the pigment itself. Case reports exist on side effects, and men weigh how natural it looks.

powder-ombre-nano-brows.text: Users choose these semi-permanent brow tattoos for a soft, shaded fill that looks like brow makeup, visible straight after the session. They are popular salon services with no dedicated studies.

chain: Plant dye stains brow hair and skin
henna-brows.text: Users get henna applied to darken and define their brows, with the stain visible immediately and lasting days to weeks. The result is a surface stain on hair and skin and is directly observable.

brow-shaving-brow-reshaping-for-tilt.text: Looksmaxxers reshape or trim brows to change how angled the eye area looks, aiming for a positive tilt or 'hunter eyes' look. The change is cheap, reversible and visible right away. Its effect on perceived tilt has not been studied.

brow-thread-lift.text: Users get threads placed to raise the tail of the brow without surgery, giving a lifted look that is visible after the procedure. It is offered as an alternative to surgical brow lifts. Evidence on how long it lasts is thin.

chain: Implant adds bony support under eye
Hollow and tear trough fill out
orbital-rim-implants.text: Hardmaxxing circles discuss silicone or porous implants along the lower orbital rim to build support under the eye and smooth hollows, a change that is visible once healed. It is promoted as more durable than fillers; published data is thin.

chain: Filler added at under-eye rim and cheekbone
infraorbital-rim-zygomatic-filler.text: Users get hyaluronic acid filler placed around the lower orbital rim and cheekbone to add support under the eyes and a more structured mid-face, visible after treatment. The result is temporary.

chain: Own fat moved into tear trough
fat-grafting-lower-eyelid-tear-trough.text: Patients use it to soften hollow under-eye areas with their own fat, giving a visibly smoother transition from lid to cheek. Evidence comes mostly from case series.

transconjunctival-lower-blepharoplasty.text: Users get it to remove or reposition under-eye fat for a flatter, less puffy lower lid, with no external scar. The result is the visible change itself once swelling settles.

plasma-pen-blepharoplasty.text: It is promoted in DIY and salon circles as a non-surgical way to tighten loose eyelid skin for a better eye area, with cheap home devices also discussed. Almost no published clinical research backs the claim.

polynucleotide-eye-filler.text: Users get polynucleotide injections around the eyes for thin, crepey lower-lid skin, aiming for better-quality, fresher skin. Very little published evidence exists for this periorbital use.

chain: Laser or RF heats eyelid skin
eyelid-rf-laser-tightening.text: Users get fractional laser or radiofrequency treatment to firm lax eyelid skin and reduce fine lines without surgery. Small studies show modest improvement; heavy laxity is usually treated surgically.

vitamin-k-eye-cream.text: It is marketed for dark circles with a vascular component, where users hope to fade the bluish look under the eyes. The sources reviewed contain no clinical studies of it for this use.

dermal-rollers-microneedling-eyes.text: Users needle the skin around the eyes hoping to thicken it and soften dark circles. Microneedling has some evidence for scars, but little is specific to the eye area.

bates-method-eye-exercises.text: Promoted since the early 1900s as a way to improve eyesight without glasses, so some users hope to look without lenses. Reviews find no objective gain in eyesight, so its appearance link rests on belief.

hair-bangs-frame-hairstyle-for-eyes.text: Users style bangs or face-framing hair to draw attention to the eyes and brow area and to shape the upper face, a visible change from the haircut itself. The claims about eye emphasis have little formal research.

eye-whitening-and-brightening.text: Looksmax.org posters argue white, bright sclera improves eye appearance through contrast, especially for brown eyes, and ask about eye drops. Little research targets this goal.

non-surgical-rhinoplasty-liquid-nose-job.text: Users get filler injected to smooth a bridge bump, lift the tip or add projection without surgery, with the change visible immediately. Results are temporary.

chain: Airway opens and nose aligns better
septoplasty.text: Septoplasty is functional surgery for breathing, but people discuss it because it can make small cosmetic changes such as to the tip, and is often combined with rhinoplasty. Alone it may not straighten a crooked-looking nose.

septorhinoplasty.text: Users have septum and outer-nose surgery together to fix breathing and reshape a crooked or unwanted nose, the visible result being the new nose shape. The evidence base is mostly surgical case series.
